## 72b99d3a9be8

**Classification: reproduced training shortcut (`A1`); target left unchanged.**

The generator claims to teach diagonal rays bouncing from color-2 walls, including orientation-dependent reflection, but its normal sampler only creates **full-width horizontal color-2 rows**. Adjacent sampled rows can form full-width multi-row slabs, yet no sampled color-2 cell belonged only to a narrow vertical wall. In a source-bound probe of 1,000 draws (generator SHA-256 `8ce0f99699a62d27d6dec57d5e9ca3cc8d8e6d189bf56cf1622db56baf55e8c5`, seed `20261007`, sample indices `0..999`, easy/default/hard cycle), the color-2 cell geometry counts were 17,059 horizontal-only, 6,239 two-dimensional slab cells, and **0 vertical-only**.

I implemented a plausible generator-specific rival: infer bounce orientation from full-width slab thickness, but treat every non-full-width wall as horizontal. It matched the selected Racket output for **64/64 generated inputs** (same seed, indices `0..63`). On canonical training pair 2, which contains a narrow vertical wall, the rival and selected Racket rule differ in **7 cells**. Thus a model can fit sampled labels by learning the generator artifact rather than the general vertical-wall branch.

The canonical counterexample is rule-lawful but does **not** pass the current target `self_check`: it touches the border, lacks the required color-3 decoy, and does not satisfy the generator-specific backward-ray checks. It is therefore outside the current implemented generator domain even though it is part of canonical authority; that mismatch is the finding.

Reproducer and hashes: `checks/audit/72b99d3a9be8/evidence.json`. Input: `checks/audit/72b99d3a9be8/input.json`. Selected Racket output: `checks/audit/72b99d3a9be8/racket.json`. Rival output: `checks/audit/72b99d3a9be8/rival-output.json`. Generated batch: `checks/audit/72b99d3a9be8/generated-batch-input.json`, `generated-batch-racket.json`, and `generated-batch-rival.json` in the same directory.

No fix was made because this was an audit-only target. A repair should add true vertical walls and retain separate horizontal/vertical branch witnesses; it should also avoid relying on adjacent full-width slabs as a surrogate for vertical geometry.
